title: PromptVersion must not write its internal tags into the caller's tags dict
answers: PromptVersion changes the tags dict I passed in
reusing a tags dict makes a new prompt get the old prompt's template or model config
prompt version tags contain mlflow.prompt.text after construction
model_config leaks from one prompt version to another
body:
Symptom: Reusing one tags dict for two prompt versions makes the second prompt show the first prompt's model config (and template tags), and the caller's dict gains mlflow.prompt.* keys.
Root cause: mlflow/entities/model_registry/prompt_version.py:PromptVersion.__init__ did `tags = tags or {}`, which aliases the caller's dict, then wrote internal tags (mlflow.prompt.text, mlflow.prompt.type, mlflow.prompt.is_prompt, model config) into it.
Fix pattern: Copy the incoming mapping before adding internal keys (`tags = dict(tags or {})`). Apply the same copy-before-write to any constructor that stores caller-supplied dicts and then adds keys.
Constraints: Applies to PromptVersion construction paths that take `tags`. Copying is shallow; nested values in the caller's dict are still shared.
applies: Any change to PromptVersion.__init__ or other entity constructors in mlflow/entities that accept a tags dict and add keys to it.
says: Creating a second prompt version unexpectedly displays model settings from the first prompt.
Saving a new prompt modifies my original labels dictionary with internal tracking fields.
New prompt versions inherit model configurations and template labels from previously registered prompts.
Ensure prompt creation does not pollute or overwrite existing custom metadata across versions.
search: Constructors in mlflow/entities, particularly PromptVersion.__init__, must copy caller-supplied tags mappings before mutating them with internal keys such as mlflow.prompt.text, mlflow.prompt.type, mlflow.prompt.is_prompt, and model config. Applies to PromptVersion construction taking tags or any entity constructor storing caller dicts; copying is shallow, leaving nested values shared.
